dimensions.assessment: Affects manufacturers of reference biologic drugs and companies developing and seeking to market biosimilar drug products.
dimensions.evidence: brings an action for infringement under this section against an applicant for approval of a biological product

dimensions.assessment: Restricts patent litigation strategies and patent counts in biosimilar patent disputes, potentially impacting drug market entry timelines and legal disputes.
dimensions.evidence: the reference product sponsor may assert in the action a total of not more than 20 patents

dimensions.assessment: May affect drug pricing and market competition for biological products, though specific fiscal or economic estimates are not provided.
Amends federal patent law (Title 35, United States Code) regarding patent infringement actions for biological products.
dimensions.evidence: Section 271(e) of title 35, United States Code, is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change applicable to biosimilar applications submitted on or after the date of enactment.
dimensions.evidence: shall apply with respect to an application submitted under section 351(k) of the Public Health Service Act... on or after the date of enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Specific economic savings or federal budget impacts
importance_detail.rationale: The bill limits the number of patents (generally to no more than 20) that a reference biologic drug manufacturer can assert in infringement lawsuits against biosimilar applicants under certain conditions. Courts may modify the limit for good cause or in the interest of justice.
